chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who married off his slave girl to a man and stipulated for him that whatever child she bears will be free; if her husband divorced her or he died, and then she was married to another man, what is the status of her child? He said: 'Her status is that he made that condition only for the first [husband], and she is at the choice of the second [husband]; if he wishes, he manumits [her child], and if he wishes, he keeps [her as a slave].'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a slave's child when the mother is remarried after a manumission condition was set by the first husband?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal nuance of conditional manumission (*tadbir*) for a slave woman (*umm al-walad*) who is remarried. The Imam establishes that the stipulation of freedom is tied to the first husband's ownership rights, granting the second husband the independent discretion (*ikhtiyar*) to either emancipate the child or retain them in servitude, reflecting the juristic principle that manumission conditions are personal to the stipulator.
